findings.claim: The requirement says all generated code gets `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`. The derived criterion allows conditional emission only where the attribute does not exist. The change wraps every attribute in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`. But `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` does exist, with AttributeTargets.Class, in .NET Framework 4.0+ and in netstandard2.0. So consumers building for net4x or netstandard2.0 (a large share of MessagePack users, including libraries) get no attribute on any generated formatter or resolver, and the requirement is not met for them.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageOnLegacyTargetsTests.GeneratedTypesAreExcludedEvenWhenLegacyTargetSymbolDefined (NETFRAMEWORK and NETSTANDARD2_0). It drives the generator with that preprocessor symbol and checks every generated class symbol carries the attribute. Expected to fail on head. The same guard appears in EnumTemplate.tt:8, UnionTemplate.tt:10, StringKeyFormatterTemplate.tt:18, ResolverTemplate.tt:14/31/48 and CompositeResolverTemplate.tt:7/35.

findings.claim: The README says the attribute is "only emitted for targets where it is available (not `netstandard2.0` or .NET Framework)". That is factually wrong: ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute is available on both. The doc documents the coverage gap as a platform limitation instead of a choice.

receipt_plan.detail: Compare with the API docs for System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute, which list .NET Framework 4.0+ and .NET Standard 2.0. Compiling `[System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] class C {}` against net472 or netstandard2.0 reference assemblies succeeds.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Always-on: every generated formatter, resolver and helper class gets [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] in all templates, with no generator option to turn it off. This is what the change implements, apart from its target-framework #if guard.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Opt-out setting, which the requirement explicitly calls acceptable: same template edits, plus a boolean on the generator options (e.g. read from an MSBuild/analyzer-config property or from the GeneratedMessagePackResolver attribute), default true. Each template wraps the attribute line in `<# if (Options.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage) { #> ... <# } #>`, so users who want coverage of generated code can disable it.
